SUNOG SA COMMONWEALTH

Umabot sa ikalimang alarma ang sunog sa Commonwealth Market sa kahabaan ng Commonwealth Avenue sa Quezon City kaninang madaling-araw ng April 25.

Sumiklab ang apoy bandang 2:00 a.m. kanina at inabot ng halos apat na oras bago idineklarang fire out dakong 6:36 a.m. ngayong umaga.

Wala namang naiulat na nasaktan o nasugatan sa insidente. Iniimbestigahan pa ang sanhi ng apoy. | via The Philippine Star

📸: Kankaloo Fire Rescue Eagles & Brgy. Tandang Sora Fire Brigade

No fire broke out about 2:00 a.m. earlier and took about four hours before the declaration of fire out of 6:36 a. This morning. No one was reported injured or injured in the incident. It investigated the cause of the fire.DU. The Philippine Staragana: Kanoorecues Eagle Brygra.

data.raw_text:
Whether you’re on a crowded bus in New York, the Tube in London, a train in Tokyo, a jeep in Manila, or stuck in traffic anywhere in the world, don’t just scroll. Pray the Rosary. Quietly. Discreetly. Powerfully🇻🇦

Pope Leo XIII, in his 1883 encyclical Supremi Apostolatus Officio, strongly encouraged all Christians to pray the Rosary “publicly or privately.” He called it “a most powerful warlike weapon” given to us by Heaven, one that puts the enemy to flight and restores faith and piety in the world.  

Pope St. John Paul II, in Rosarium Virginis Mariae (2002), reminded us that the Rosary “marks the rhythm of human life” and remains a powerful tool for evangelization. When prayed with the heart, even in the middle of a busy commute, it proclaims the Gospel right where people live and move.  

St. Josemaría Escrivá gave perfect advice for modern life:  “If there is no other time, say it in the street without letting anybody notice it. It will, moreover, help you to have presence of God.”  

That’s the hidden power of praying the Rosary in public:  

🌹 You carry Christ straight into the heart of daily chaos.  

🌹 You invite Our Lady’s powerful intercession exactly where it’s needed most.  

🌹 You transform ordinary travel time into sacred time, turning buses, trains, subways, and airports into places of prayer.  

No one even has to see your rosary beads (you can use your fingers). But Heaven notices.  

The world is noisy, distracted, and often dark. Let’s bring the light of the Rosary into it, one decade at a time.  

The Rosary belongs in our streets, our commutes, and our busy lives. Let’s take it there.
